items.title: Along Himalayan Floods’ Path, Wiped Out Towns and Mounting Grief
items.summary: Survivors tell the stories of the people and places buried under the mud after a disaster in Nepal.

items.title: Tracing the Path of Nepal’s Flood
items.summary: Mujib Mashal, our South Asia bureau chief, travels to points along a river in Nepal that turned into a deadly torrent, killing more than 1,300 people and leaving over 5,000 more missing as entire, towns bridges and roads were swept away.

items.title: An Election in Sweden Shows Shifting Priorities
items.summary: Sweden votes on Sunday. With various crises easing, center-left politics seem in vogue again, but the far right cannot be discounted.

items.title: Iran Finds Escalation Is Fruitful Path to Leverage in War With U.S.
items.summary: Iran and its allies now hold sway over two key oil shipping routes, and Tehran is setting the stage for a diplomatic win that could enhance its stature.

items.title: Trump Says Irish Unification Would Be ‘Fantastic,’ Breaking With Precedent
items.summary: The United States has been officially neutral on an issue that was a source of decades of violence in Northern Ireland until a 1998 peace deal.

items.title: In Doonbeg, Trump’s Irish Open Visit Prompts Protests and Praise
items.summary: As the U.S. president heads to his Doonbeg hotel for the Irish Open, locals expressed both appreciation for the resort’s economic benefits and opposition to his politics.

items.title: Saudi Arabia’s Oil ‘Lifeline’ Was Attacked. Here’s What to Know.
items.summary: A drone attack from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to close its East-West pipeline, the kingdom said, threatening a key workaround to Iran’s Persian Gulf blockade.

items.title: Death Toll From Ferry Fire in the Philippines Rises to 76
items.summary: Rescuers were still searching for victims days after a fire broke out on the June Aster en route to a popular tourist site. At least 43 people survived.

items.title: In Flood-Stricken Nepal, a Cool Gust Carries Hopes of a Miracle Rescue
items.summary: Rescuers clawing through a hydropower tunnel clogged with mud, water and rock have found a pocket of air near where six workers are believed to be trapped.

items.title: ‘We Left in the Clothes We Were Wearing’: Yemenis Flee New Fighting
items.summary: Hunger and disease have tormented Yemen for years. Now, fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Iran-backed Houthis is pushing it to the brink.

items.title: How The Times Covers ‘60 Minutes’ and Other Journalists
items.summary: Journalists don’t want to become the story. But newsrooms — and the people who run them — are the story for Times media reporters.

items.title: Risks for Clicks: Why Online Influencers Push Shock Content
items.summary: A growing number of social media creators are pushing the boundaries of safety and good taste to feed algorithms and win followers.

items.title: After the I.P.O., a Billion-Dollar Bill for Employee Paydays
items.summary: A compensation strategy at start-ups keeps expenses low until they go public. At that point, the companies may face billions of dollars in catch-up expenses.

items.title: Inflation Complicates Trump’s Midterms Pitch to Voters
items.summary: Gas prices are high, mortgage rates are climbing and inflation remains well above target, complicating the president’s midterm appeal.

items.title: How to Lure the Spendy and the Thrifty? Bring On the ‘Barbell.’
items.summary: Restaurant chains are trying to draw in both kinds of consumers by offering low-cost and more-premium options at the same time.

items.title: Want to Entice New Residents? Offer Cash, for a Start.
items.summary: Relocation incentives have a mixed record of helping cities and towns stand out as people return to rural America.

items.title: India Wants to Buy Fewer Chinese Imports, but Keeps Needing More
items.summary: Trade between India and China has nearly doubled in five years, leaving New Delhi with a widening deficit and a difficult choice over how to build its industrial future.

items.title: Saudi Oil Exports Face Heightened Threats After Attacks on Pipeline
items.summary: Ship operators already faced severe risks in navigating the region, and now the danger is higher as Houthi militias assert control in the Red Sea.

items.title: Court Strikes Down Trump Order to Keep an Aging Coal-Burning Plant Running
items.summary: The 64-year-old Michigan power plant was set to retire. Then the Trump administration intervened in a way that overstepped its authority, a court ruled.

items.title: AARP Projects 2027 Social Security COLA at 3.6%
items.summary: If the AARP’s projection holds, the cost-of-living adjustment would be the largest since 2023.

items.title: Anthropic C.E.O. Dario Amodei Calls for A.I. Slowdown
items.summary: In an essay, the head of Anthropic laid out the rapidly advancing capabilities of artificial intelligence and said there needed to be greater safety controls across the industry.

items.title: Inside the Discussions at AI Companies Over a Superintelligence Doomsday
items.summary: Researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google are increasingly trying to raise awareness about the risks of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Why It’s Difficult for Tech Companies to Rein In A.I.
items.summary: Researchers say artificial intelligence is developing faster than the systems put in place to monitor and control it.

items.title: How Minnesota Became the Front Line in the Fight Over Prediction Markets
items.summary: The state was the first to pass a law banning Kalshi and Polymarket. A lawsuit filed by a federal agency may set a precedent on who gets to regulate them.

items.title: The Mic Is On. So Is Live Auto-Tune.
items.summary: As audiences demand perfection from live performances, pitch correction technology has become an increasingly common way for singers to deliver.

items.title: Elon Musk Has Pledged to Rid His Platform, X, of Child Sexual Abuse, but It Persists
items.summary: Reviews by the Canadian Center for Child Protection and The New York Times found that explicit images of children remain on the social media site owned by Elon Musk.

items.title: The Ezra Klein Show: The A.I. Revolt Is Here
items.summary: The A.I. giants weren’t prepared for this.

items.title: Could A.I. Really Kill All Humans?
items.summary: After an Anthropic researcher quit, warning that the A.I. race is “gambling with our lives,” Cade Metz joined Natalie Kitroeff on “The Call” to break down what’s at stake.

items.title: California’s Governor Signs Landmark Online Child Safety Bills
items.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a bill that prohibits social media platforms from providing addictive features to users under 16, the first law of its kind in the nation.

items.title: Anthropic Says It Blocked Possible Efforts to Build Biological Weapons
items.summary: In a new report, the A.I. start-up added that it could not determine whether the research was legitimate or nefarious, leading the company to shut down the work.
